scope: Modern Exteriors only (assets/limezu/ext/). Interiors / Modern Office out of scope.
_doc: L1 semantics layer of the exterior placement brain. This file is the single
source of truth for the vocabularies the enrichment pass (W1-A), the group
recipes (W1-C) and the district compiler (W2-A) share: roles, surfaces,
mounts, biomes, palettes, interactions, density and slots.
Nothing here places anything by itself. The compiler reads a district spec
(see example_district_spec), resolves biome + palette + slots + density,
then draws candidates from the enriched me.*/exs.* catalog filtered by the
Coordinate conventions match data/city-plan.json: world pixels, 16px tile
grid, stamp anchors bl (default) / bc / tl, and stamp depth defaulting to

roles._doc: Role = what an asset structurally IS for placement purposes, independent of its theme. Every me.* gets exactly one role. `categories` lists the registry.jsonl `category` values that auto-map to this role in W1-A; `tags_any` narrows within a category.

ground_fill.label: Ground fill
ground_fill.desc: Terrain autotiles and large flat slabs that paint the district floor. Emitted as `patches`, not as stamps.

ground_edge.label: Ground edge / transition
ground_edge.desc: Curbs, shorelines, cliff faces, surface-to-surface transition strips. Must straddle the boundary between two surfaces.

road_marking.label: Road marking
road_marking.desc: Painted lane lines, crosswalks, arrows, parking bays. Asphalt only, flush with the road grid.

landmark.label: Landmark
landmark.desc: Hero structure that defines a district silhouette (lighthouse, chapel, hangar, station hall, big top). One or two per district; placed first, everything else yields to it.

building_shell.label: Building shell
building_shell.desc: A complete building stamp that stands on the ground plane and faces the street. Doors south by default (structure-grammar.md).

facade.label: Facade module
facade.desc: Modular wall / window / balcony pieces that compose a building face. Never a solo stamp: only valid inside a grp.* recipe that also supplies roof + entrance.

roof.label: Roof module
roof.desc: Roof plates, ridges, gutters and parapets that cap a facade stack. Group-only, drawn above the facade it belongs to.

roof_prop.label: Rooftop prop
roof_prop.desc: HVAC units, antennas, water tanks, chimneys, solar panels, rooftop gardens. Must overlap a building stamp — never open ground (see audit-placement-logic.py ROOF rule).

canopy.label: Canopy / overhang
canopy.desc: Awnings, marquees, parasols, tarps, market tents, bus-stop shelters. Overhangs the walkable surface in front of a facade or over furniture, so it draws above ground props but keeps the tile walkable.

entrance.label: Entrance
entrance.desc: Doors, stoops, steps, gates, garage doors, turnstiles. The interactive seam between exterior and interior; anchors portals in the merged plan.

wall_mount.label: Wall-mounted
wall_mount.desc: Hanging shop signs, posters, graffiti panels, wall lamps, mailslots. Must abut a building face within ~24px above its baseline (audit-placement-logic.py WALL rule).

signage.label: Freestanding sign
signage.desc: Pole signs, direction poles, notice boards, price totems, district signs. Stands on the ground beside a path.

street_furn.label: Street furniture
street_furn.desc: Benches, bins, hydrants, bollards, mailboxes, ATMs, phone booths, lamp posts, planters, bike racks. Lines sidewalks against walls and road edges — never floating (structure-grammar.md).

vegetation.label: Vegetation
vegetation.desc: Trees, palms, bushes, hedges, flower beds, crops, potted greenery. Softens grass/sand and divides paved blocks as hedge rows.

barrier.label: Barrier
barrier.desc: Fences, railings, hedge dividers, jersey barriers, sandbag walls, chain-link runs. Placed as a linear run along a slot edge, not as scatter.

infra.label: Infrastructure
infra.desc: Traffic lights, utility poles, transformers, manholes, hydro boxes, pipes, tracks, platforms, pylons. Functional city plumbing that reads as permanent.
infra.notes: Piers, docks and boardwalks are the water-surface members of this role and are the one case where collision is none (they are walkable).

vehicle.label: Vehicle
vehicle.desc: Cars, trucks, buses, trains, boats, bikes, service vehicles. Faces the lane it sits in; parked ones align to a bay.

furniture_ext.label: Outdoor furniture
furniture_ext.desc: Cafe tables and chairs, sun loungers, picnic sets, bar counters, market stall tables, deck chairs. The main sit-interact population.

play_sport.label: Play / sport
play_sport.desc: Playground equipment, volleyball nets, courts, goals, pool ladders, gym rigs. Needs a clear apron of open surface around it.

decor_small.label: Small decor / clutter
decor_small.desc: Buckets, crates, toys, litter, cones, rocks, pumpkins, tools, towels. The scatter layer that makes a district look inhabited.

decal.label: Ground decal
decal.desc: Flat marks on the floor: puddles, stains, tire tracks, ground graffiti, sand ripples, footprints. Never collides, always under stamps.

water_prop.label: Water prop
water_prop.desc: Buoys, floats, moored boats, jetski, wave foam props. Must sit on a water patch or animBand (audit-placement-logic.py WATER rule).

npc_anchor.label: NPC anchor
npc_anchor.desc: Not a sprite: a compiler-emitted marker for vendor posts, queue spots, bench seats and patrol waypoints. Feeds `npcs` in the plan and (later) Denizen assign_task routes.

fragment.label: Fragment
fragment.desc: Partial cutout that is meaningless alone (half an arch, a wall corner, one awning stripe, an autotile inner piece). Tier D coverage: usable only inside a grp.* recipe, never stamped solo.

surfaces._doc: The five ground surfaces the renderer can paint (src/full-world.js TILE_KEYS + water animBands). `registry_aliases` fold the 22 free-text `surface` values in registry.jsonl onto these five during W1-A enrichment.

grass.label: Grass
grass.notes: Default world floor. Per structure-grammar.md grass must NOT show between urban-core buildings — it is for parks, hedge dividers, rooftop gardens and rural edges. The `rock` alias covers the cliff/bank pieces in 1_Terrains_and_Fences, which top out on natural ground.

sand.label: Sand
sand.notes: Beach and desert-worksite floor; meets water through the shoreline foam tile.

sidewalk.label: Sidewalk / paved
sidewalk.notes: The urban city floor. Fills all space between roads and buildings in the paved core.

asphalt.label: Asphalt road
asphalt.notes: Driving lanes are 3-4 tiles wide. Solids must never cover a lane (check-city-plan.py ROADBLOCK).

water.label: Water
water.notes: Emitted as `animBands` (animated ocean/pool), not a static patch. Blocks walking; only water_prop, boat-tagged vehicles and pier/boardwalk infra may sit on it.

mounts._doc: Non-ground attachment surfaces. An asset with a mount is positioned relative to another stamp rather than to the floor, so it can never be scattered by the fill passes.

air.label: Overhead / floating
air.notes: Cables, string lights, hanging banners spanning between two anchors.

none.label: Not placeable
none.notes: UI chrome and sheet legends; excluded from all fill passes.

biomes._doc: L3 world model. A district spec names one biome; the biome fixes which themes are drawable, which surfaces exist, palette affinity order and the forbidden token list that the QA biome-violation check (W4-C) enforces.

universal.label: Universal kit
universal.desc: Cross-biome asset kits — terrain autotiles, fences, vehicles, generic props. Always drawable as a secondary source in every biome.

urban_core.label: Urban core
urban_core.desc: Continuous paved downtown: tight building rows flush to the sidewalk, awnings over the walk, dense street furniture, no visible grass.

commercial.label: Commercial strip
commercial.desc: Shopping centre, food market and garage-sale frontage: stalls, awnings, price signage, shopper NPC anchors.

civic.label: Civic / institutional
civic.desc: School, hospital, police, fire and post office blocks: wide entrances, flagpoles, service vehicle bays, formal planting.

residential.label: Residential
residential.desc: Houses and villas with yards, driveways, fenced gardens, garage sales, loose spacing and visible grass between plots.

transit.label: Transit
transit.desc: Train and subway stations: rail beds, platforms, turnstiles, timetable boards, waiting benches, bus bays.

industrial.label: Industrial / worksite
industrial.desc: Worksite and yard: scaffolds, pipes, cones, spoil heaps, machinery, chain-link runs, rust everywhere.

military.label: Military base
military.desc: Barracks, hangars, helipads, sandbag walls, checkpoints, olive vehicles on a hard-standing.

park.label: Park / garden
park.desc: Managed greenery: lawns, flower beds, paths, gazebos, fountains, benches, hedges, playgrounds.

beach.label: Beach
beach.desc: Sand shelf against animated water: palms, loungers, parasols, bars, stages, lighthouse, buckets and toys as scatter.

leisure.label: Leisure / pool
leisure.desc: Swimming pool and resort deck: tiled water, ladders, loungers, changing cabins, tropical planting.

wild.label: Wild / camping
wild.desc: Forest clearing and campground: tents, firepits, log benches, dirt tracks, dense conifers, caravans.

rural.label: Rural / farm
rural.desc: Farm edge: crop rows, barns, wooden fences, tractors, dirt paths, hay. Uses the camping/garden/terrain kits until a dedicated farm sheet exists.

memorial.label: Memorial / graveyard
memorial.desc: Cemetery: gravestone rows, crypts, iron fencing, bare trees, lanterns, pumpkins. Somber palette, strict row alignment.

theme_biomes._doc: All 24 LimeZu Modern Exteriors theme sheets mapped to a primary biome plus the biomes that may borrow from them. W1-A seeds every me.* biome from its `sheet` via this map, then filename/tag rules refine it.

palettes._doc: Color-variant steering. LimeZu ships most props in colour families; `tokens` are the colour words that actually appear in exs.* ids (weight = affinity 0..1), `avoid` demotes a variant to last resort. W1-B turns these into a per-variant score so a district reads as one coherent colour story instead of a rainbow.

night_neon.label: Night neon
night_neon.notes: Only for lit signage / late-night blocks; never the base palette of a whole district.

interact._doc: L6 runtime contract. The compiler writes `interact` onto a stamp; W4-A wires these to handlers in src/full-world.js. `runtime` says whether the hook exists yet — the compiler may emit planned types, but QA warns instead of failing.

sit.label: Sit
sit.desc: Player (or NPC) occupies a seat facing the implied direction.

enter.label: Enter
enter.desc: Teleports through a portal into an interior scene or subway band.

read.label: Read
read.desc: Shows a text panel: district signs, notice boards, timetables, gravestones, posters.

shop.label: Shop
shop.desc: Opens a vendor exchange at a stall, counter, cart or vending machine.

play.label: Play
play.desc: Triggers a mini-interaction on playground and sport equipment.

board.label: Board
board.desc: Boards a train, bus or boat — a transit-flavoured enter that moves the player between districts.

density._doc: Fill intensity per role per slot. `target_coverage` is the fraction of the slot's free area the pass tries to occupy; `min_spacing_mult` scales the role's own spacing_px; `props_per_kilopx2` is the scatter budget per 1000 px^2 of slot area (16px tiles => 1 tile ~= 0.26 kilopx2).

slots._doc: Named regions a district spec declares (or the compiler derives from patches/roads). Each fill pass targets slots, so a rule never has to know absolute coordinates.

rules.why: Terrain autotiles are floor paint, not stamps; stamping them creates the seam artefacts listed in EXTERIOR-MISTAKES.md.
Curbs and cliff faces only make sense straddling a surface boundary.
Paint belongs on the driving surface and must never block a lane.
structure-grammar.md: all buildings face the street with doors south.
Hero structures are placed before everything else so props can yield to them.
Modular facade pieces read as floating walls when stamped alone; they must come from a grp.* recipe.
A roof without its facade stack is a floating lid.
audit-placement-logic.py flags these as misplaced whenever they sit on open ground.
Wall art must abut a building face within 24px of its baseline.
Awnings overhang the sidewalk: they must draw above the props under them but keep the tile walkable.
Entrances are the only legitimate anchor for a portal into an interior scene.
Blade and box signs whose registry surface is the wall itself are mounts, not freestanding poles.
Pole signs stand on the ground and want a path within 64px to be readable.
Catch-all for functional city plumbing (traffic lights, poles, transformers, platforms, piers, ladders) before the narrower street-furniture and canopy tag rules refine it.
structure-grammar.md: props line the sidewalks against walls and road edges, never floating.
Trees and beds want organic jitter, not tile lock, and they block movement.
Everything in the fence/wall kits is a linear run along a slot edge; scattered fence pieces are the classic broken look.
Railings and barriers filed under other categories (school railing, military sandbags) still have to be run out as a line, not scattered.
Piers and boardwalks are walkable structures laid over water or sand, so they must not inherit the fence kit's barrier collision.
A car on grass reads as a bug; vehicles snap to a lane, bay, yard, rail bed or water.
audit-placement-logic.py WATER rule: hulls and buoys must sit on a water band.
Outdoor furniture is the main sit-interact population and looks best slightly off-grid.
Play equipment needs a clear apron or it reads as clutter.
Decals are floor paint: fixed depth under every stamp, no collision.
Catch-all scatter layer; this is where the bulk of the unused 6224 Singles gets spent.
LimeZu `Example_*` cutouts are pre-assembled scenes; treat them as ready-made groups, not as generic props.
Tier D coverage: autotile fragments are only legal inside a group recipe.
Sheet NPCs are population hints, not stamps; they become `npcs` entries.
Sheet legends and UI chrome must never enter a fill pass.

example_rules._doc: Worked examples showing a fully resolved rule for one asset — what W1-A enrichment should produce per me.* id.

me.beach.palm_tree.name: Palm tree
me.beach.palm_tree.notes: Single detailed palm, 64x80 with a 4-tile canopy. Collides on the trunk only, so the 24x12 footprint is narrower than the sprite. Cluster in 2-3s with >=56px trunk spacing so canopies overlap without stacking trunks; keep >=32px off the shoreline foam tile and never on the sidewalk boardwalk.

example_district_spec._doc: Shape of a compiler-driven district (W2-B `d18-beach-compiler-pilot.json`). The compiler consumes this plus placement-rules.json and emits the usual patches/roads/stamps/anims/solids/portals/npcs fragment that merge-city-plan.py already understands. Hand `stamps` arrays stay legal for pinned hero placements.

keep_clear.why: walk-down from the promenade to the water
